title: Using ggmtools with other methods
text: JGL package archived CRAN July 2025; install CRAN archive remotes::install_github("cran/JGL"). returns list whose theta element holds one precision matrix per group. Tune two penalties ggm_bic(), BIC used JGL Koyejo lab code (smaller better): Refit chosen penalties. ggmtools pcor_estimate() method JGL fits, converts precision matrix precision_to_pcor(). JGL store group names, pass , fit return.whole.theta = TRUE every variable kept: fused penalty sets many differences exactly 0. diff_edge_table() lists rest shared edge-table format: JGL unregularized estimate agree edges change ? JGL ties every edge fuses difference exactly 0, topk_overlap() counts ties fairly instead edge position: simulation, true graphs known, estimates go straight roc_auc(), pr_auc() confusion_at_threshold(), abs(pcor$Normal) (threshold_to_adjacency(fit$theta[[1]], 1e-8)) score true adjacency matrix truth.
code: library(ggmtools) library(JGL)  grid <- expand.grid(lambda1 = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3),                     lambda2 = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1)) grid$bic <- apply(grid, 1, function(g) {   fit <- JGL(brca_pi3k, penalty = "fused", lambda1 = g[["lambda1"]],              lambda2 = g[["lambda2"]], return.whole.theta = TRUE)   ggm_bic(brca_pi3k, fit$theta) }) best <- grid[which.min(grid$bic), ] best #>   lambda1 lambda2      bic #> 2     0.1    0.01 29.43266 fit <- JGL(brca_pi3k, penalty = "fused", lambda1 = best$lambda1,            lambda2 = best$lambda2, return.whole.theta = TRUE) genes <- colnames(brca_pi3k$Normal) pcor <- pcor_estimate(fit, groupnames = names(brca_pi3k))  # Number of edges in each group's graph sapply(fit$theta, function(theta) sum(threshold_to_adjacency(theta, 1e-8)) / 2) #> [1] 123 149 d <- diff_edge_table(pcor$Normal, pcor$Tumor, threshold = 1e-8, varnames = genes) nrow(d) #> [1] 201 head(d[order(-abs(d$diff)), ]) #>      i  j  node1   node2      est_g1     est_g2       diff #> 7    3  6   AKT2 MAPKAP1  0.38552727  0.0000000  0.3855273 #> 90   9 19   PDK1  INPP4B -0.04251113 -0.3683474  0.3258362 #> 80   8 18   MTOR  DEPDC5  0.02470883  0.3490456 -0.3243367 #> 107  2 21 AKT1S1   NPRL3  0.29674004  0.0000000  0.2967400 #> 169 17 26  RPTOR   STK11  0.29551205  0.0000000  0.2955121 #> 180 10 27 PIK3CA    TSC1  0.27580379  0.0000000  0.2758038 pcor_inv <- lapply(brca_pi3k, function(x) precision_to_pcor(solve(cov(x)))) k <- c(10, 25, 50, 100, 200) data.frame(k = k,            overlap = topk_overlap(abs(pcor$Normal - pcor$Tumor),                                   abs(pcor_inv$Normal - pcor_inv$Tumor), k)) #>     k overlap #> 1  10       3 #> 2  25       4 #> 3  50      15 #> 4 100      35 #> 5 200     110

title: Using ggmtools with other methods
text: mGHS (Busatto & Stingo 2025) fitted multiGGM multiggm_mcmc(method = "mghs"). fit multiGGM fit, ggmtools generics work directly. horseshoe prior point mass zero, multiGGM defines edge probability shrinkage weights, P(wk,ij>0.5)P(w_{k,ij} > 0.5) w=λ2/(1+λ2)w = \lambda^2 / (1 + \lambda^2); see multiGGM documentation.
code: library(multiGGM) fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = brca_pi3k, method = "mghs")  pips <- pip_table(fit)       # long table: i, j, node1, node2, group, pip pcor <- pcor_estimate(fit)   # list of partial-correlation matrices  normal <- pips[pips$group == "Normal", ] normal$selected <- bayes_fdr(normal$pip, alpha = 0.05)

title: Using ggmtools with other methods
text: pip_table() pcor_estimate() form common interface. Supporting new method means writing adapter: S3 methods convert fitted object shared output. ggmtools ships adapter JGL fits (class "jgl"), template others. hypothetical method whose fits class "mymethod" store list precision matrices fit$precision: script, defining function enough dispatch. package, register S3method(ggmtools::pcor_estimate, mymethod) NAMESPACE (roxygen: @exportS3Method ggmtools::pcor_estimate). method returns posterior probabilities can build pip_table() output as_pip_table().
code: pcor_estimate.mymethod <- function(fit, varnames = NULL, groupnames = NULL, ...) {   out <- lapply(fit$precision, precision_to_pcor)   p <- nrow(out[[1]])   varnames <- if (!is.null(varnames)) varnames else     if (!is.null(rownames(out[[1]]))) rownames(out[[1]]) else paste0("V", seq_len(p))   out <- lapply(out, function(m) { dimnames(m) <- list(varnames, varnames); m })   names(out) <- if (!is.null(groupnames)) groupnames else     paste0("Group_", seq_along(out))   out }

text: Shared tools R packages estimate multiple Gaussian graphical models (GGMs), currently spikeyglass: Bayesian joint spike--slab graphical lasso (Li, McCormick & Clark 2019), fitted EM; multiGGM: Bayesian multiple GGMs MCMC: G-Wishart Markov random field prior (Peterson, Stingo & Vannucci 2015), scalable spike--slab (scale-multiGGM; Shaddox et al. 2018), multi-platform (Shaddox et al. 2020) multiple graphical horseshoe (mGHS; Busatto & Stingo 2025). packages import ggmtools re-export users call, functions objects whichever package attached one downstream script works fits either. functions take plain matrices (precision, partial-correlation, score adjacency matrices) vectors p-values probabilities, fitted objects. work just well estimator, joint graphical lasso (JGL), graphical lasso random-forest importance score: see Using ggmtools methods.

what: Example: differential edges in the TCGA data
title: Shared Tools for Multiple Gaussian Graphical Model Packages
text: brca_pi3k holds standardized expression 28 PI3K-pathway genes 100 normal 100 tumour breast samples. n > p, inverse sample covariance gives simple (unregularized) estimate group’s partial correlations. differences larger chance? Permuting group labels gives null distribution |difference|; pooling edges gives fine-grained p-values. 100 samples per group regularization, difference survives BH correction 378 edges. joint estimators spikeyglass multiGGM borrow strength across groups tools use real analysis; two calls test estimates. Bayesian method gives posterior probabilities instead, e.g. P(edge differs). bayes_fdr() selects largest set edges whose posterior expected FDR target (tied probabilities kept together):
code: library(ggmtools)  pcor <- lapply(brca_pi3k, function(x) precision_to_pcor(solve(cov(x)))) d <- diff_edge_table(pcor$Normal, pcor$Tumor, threshold = 0.3) head(d[order(-abs(d$diff)), ]) #>     i  j  node1   node2     est_g1      est_g2       diff #> 37  2 21 AKT1S1   NPRL3  0.4344316 -0.16654190  0.6009735 #> 33  8 18   MTOR  DEPDC5 -0.1053410  0.47261097 -0.5779520 #> 23  3 15   AKT2    RPS6 -0.5468767  0.02156526 -0.5684420 #> 51 13 24   RHEB PPP2R1A  0.3695557 -0.18810932  0.5576650 #> 47  4 24   AKT3 PPP2R1A  0.3664210 -0.16630078  0.5327218 #> 5   3  6   AKT2 MAPKAP1  0.3845418 -0.14658324  0.5311250 set.seed(1) X <- rbind(brca_pi3k$Normal, brca_pi3k$Tumor) diff_score <- function(rows) {   p1 <- precision_to_pcor(solve(cov(X[rows, ])))   p2 <- precision_to_pcor(solve(cov(X[-rows, ])))   abs(p1 - p2) } observed <- diff_score(1:100) null <- replicate(100, diff_score(sample(200, 100)), simplify = FALSE)  pp <- pooled_perm_pvalues(observed, null) edges <- cbind(diff_edge_table(pcor$Normal, pcor$Tumor, threshold = -Inf),                pvalue = pp$pvalue, p_adj = pp$p_adj) head(edges[order(edges$pvalue), c("node1", "node2", "diff", "pvalue", "p_adj")]) #>      node1   node2       diff      pvalue    p_adj #> 192 AKT1S1   NPRL3  0.6009735 0.004550144 0.604984 #> 144   MTOR  DEPDC5 -0.5779520 0.006507764 0.604984 #> 94    AKT2    RPS6 -0.5684420 0.007380757 0.604984 #> 266   RHEB PPP2R1A  0.5576650 0.008491839 0.604984 #> 257   AKT3 PPP2R1A  0.5327218 0.011851538 0.604984 #> 13    AKT2 MAPKAP1  0.5311250 0.012010264 0.604984 sum(edges$p_adj < 0.05) #> [1] 0 prob <- c(0.999, 0.99, 0.97, 0.97, 0.80, 0.40, 0.05) bayes_fdr(prob, alpha = 0.05) #> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE FALSE #> attr(,"expected_fdr") #> [1] 0.01775 #> attr(,"n_selected") #> [1] 4 #> attr(,"cutoff") #> [1] 0.97 #> attr(,"alpha") #> [1] 0.05

what: Example: evaluating an estimate against a known graph
title: Shared Tools for Multiple Gaussian Graphical Model Packages
text: simulation true precision matrix known. , chain graph 20 variables, estimated 40 samples: ROC PR curves step distinct score values, sparse estimators, tie many edges exactly 0, get AUC depend order variables. sparse estimate, also compare pr_auc(..., method = "average_precision"): default trapezoid draws straight line across large tied block, optimistic.
code: set.seed(3) p <- 20 Omega <- diag(p) Omega[cbind(1:(p - 1), 2:p)] <- Omega[cbind(2:p, 1:(p - 1))] <- 0.3 X <- matrix(rnorm(40 * p), 40) %*% chol(solve(Omega))  Omega_hat <- solve(cov(X)) score <- abs(precision_to_pcor(Omega_hat))   # edge score: |partial correlation| truth <- threshold_to_adjacency(Omega, threshold = 0)  roc_auc(score, truth)$auc #> [1] 0.8024007 pr_auc(score, truth)$auc #> [1] 0.3226991 cm <- confusion_at_threshold(score, truth, threshold = 0.3) unlist(cm[c("TP", "FP", "TPR", "FDR", "MCC")]) #>         TP         FP        TPR        FDR        MCC  #> 11.0000000 23.0000000  0.5789474  0.6764706  0.3478489 kl_divergence(Omega_hat, solve(Omega)) #> [1] 6.767717 relative_frobenius(Omega_hat, Omega) #> [1] 2.173401 sparse <- score * (score > 0.3)      # e.g. a thresholded or lasso-type estimate mean(sparse[upper.tri(sparse)] == 0) # share of edges tied at 0 #> [1] 0.8210526 c(trapezoid = pr_auc(sparse, truth)$auc,   average_precision = pr_auc(sparse, truth, method = "average_precision")$auc) #>         trapezoid average_precision  #>         0.3188026         0.2854237

what: BIC for multiple Gaussian graphical models — ggm_bic
title: BIC for multiple Gaussian graphical models — ggm_bic
text: BIC-type criterion tuning joint estimators K precision matrices (e.g. penalties joint graphical lasso), summed groups: $$\sum_k \left[\mathrm{tr}(S_k\hat\Theta_k) - \log|\hat\Theta_k| +   \frac{\log n_k}{n_k} E_k\right],$$ \(S_k\) sample covariance group \(k\) (denominator \(n_k - 1\)), \(n_k\) sample size \(E_k\) number entries \(\hat\Theta_k\) \(|\hat\theta_{ij}| \ge\) threshold. \(E_k\) counts every entry matrix, including diagonal triangles. per-observation form used Koyejo lab joint graphical lasso code (vBIC()); smaller better.

title: BIC for multiple Gaussian graphical models — ggm_bic
BIC for multiple Gaussian graphical models — ggm_bic
text: data_list List K data matrices (\(n_k\) x p). theta_list List K estimated p x p precision matrices. threshold Entries absolute value >= threshold count non-zero. Default 0.001.

title: Precision-recall curve and AUPR for edge recovery — pr_auc
text: Three summaries curve available: "trapezoid" Trapezoid rule curve points, starting precision 1 recall 0. matches tie-corrected compute_aupr() DiNA simulation. straight line across large tied block achievable PR space, optimistic sparse estimators tie many edges 0. "average_precision" Step-wise average precision, \(\sum_b (R_b - R_{b-1}) P_b\) tie blocks \(b\), scikit-learn. tied block contributes precision whole block. "interpolated" Exact area curve obtained interpolating true false positives linearly within tied block (Davis & Goadrich 2006; continuous version, PRROC package). Precision linear recall within block, differs trapezoid. Without ties, "average_precision" "interpolated" close; large tied blocks "trapezoid" can much larger . Edges missing score truth dropped.

title: ggmtools 0.0.0.9000
text: Method-agnostic helpers moved DiNA simulation (dina_simulation/04_calc_metrics.R, 00_helper_functions.R, tcga_demo/utils.R), overlapping versions spikeyglass multiGGMr merged one. New: pr_auc() (PR curve AUPR; method = "trapezoid", "average_precision" "interpolated"), topk_overlap(), bayes_fdr(), pooled_perm_pvalues(), relative_frobenius(), kl_divergence(), ggm_bic(), threshold_to_adjacency(), diff_adjacency(), upper_tri_to_matrix() diff_edge_table(). confusion_at_threshold() also returns FDR MCC. confusion_at_threshold(), roc_auc() pr_auc() accept vectors edge scores truths well p x p matrices. stats added Imports. New pcor_estimate() method joint graphical lasso fits JGL::JGL() (class "jgl"). reads fit$theta, ggmtools depend JGL. Fits must use return.whole.theta = TRUE. Old new names: Behaviour differences old versions: bayes_fdr() keeps tied probabilities together: cutoff placed distinct values, selection longer depends input order. whole tie block push expected FDR alpha, none selected. Example: prob = c(1, 1, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9), alpha = 0.05 used select 4 edges (two three tied 0.9s, chosen position); now selects 2. Results without ties cutoff unchanged. pooled_perm_pvalues() spikeyglass’s version: null value counts exceedance within relative tolerance (sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) * max(1, |x|)) observed score. DiNA subtracted absolute .Machine$double.eps, vanishes scores >= 2, exact ties counted. Example: observed 3 null c(1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4) gave p = 2/7 now gives 5/7. Without ties p-values unchanged. returns pvalue p_adj (DiNA: pvalues, p_adj, upper_tri_idx; use edge_index(p) indices). kl_divergence() returns Kullback-Leibler divergence KL(N(0, Sigma) || N(0, theta_hat^-1)) = (tr(Sigma theta_hat) - log|Sigma theta_hat| - p) / 2. DiNA’s compute_kl_divergence() omitted 1/2 (Stein’s loss), values twice kl_divergence(); comment also direction reversed. Rankings unchanged. singular theta_hat gives NA instead Inf. ggm_bic() equals vBIC() valid input; returns NA estimated precision matrix missing values zero negative determinant (vBIC() used log|det| ignored sign). takes list precision matrices, fitted JGL object. pr_auc() default method = "trapezoid" equals DiNA’s tie-corrected compute_aupr(). "average_precision" "interpolated" (Davis-Goadrich) new; trapezoid optimistic large tied block (e.g. edges exactly 0) lower precision edges . precision_to_pcor() symmetrizes result returns NA warning non-positive diagonal; DiNA’s pcor_from_precision() kept asymmetry returned NaN. diff_edge_table() returns shared edge-table columns , j, node1, node2, est_g1, est_g2, diff upper.tri() order. DiNA’s extract_diff_edges() returned gene1, gene2, pcor_group1, pcor_group2, diff, sorted -abs(diff). topk_overlap() counts overlap two top-k lists ties broken random expectation. Taking order(...)[1:k], DiNA’s plot_topk_overlap() , breaks ties position, inflates overlap sparse methods k exceeds non-zero edges.

title: ggmtools 0.0.0.9000
text: Initial version. Collects functions previously duplicated spikeyglass multiGGMr (precision_to_pcor(), confusion_at_threshold(), roc_auc(), plot_roc()), one signature, plus shared generics pip_table() pcor_estimate(), edge-table helpers edge_index() as_pip_table(), brca_pi3k dataset. roc_auc() handles tied scores correctly: curve steps distinct scores, AUC equals Mann-Whitney statistic. (multiGGMr’s previous version accumulated one edge time, tied edges ordered matrix position.) returns auc (lower case). confusion_at_threshold() returns list including precision F1. Rates zero denominator NA.
